# Warp — Complete AI Reference

> Distributed job processing, message queue, and in-memory mediator library for .NET 10.

Warp provides three patterns — Messages (pub/sub), Jobs (orchestrated background work), and Requests (in-memory mediator) — through a unified pipeline. It uses the transactional outbox pattern: jobs are committed atomically with business data in the same DbContext. No separate message broker required.

Ships as NuGet packages: Moberg.Warp.Core (also includes always-on durable outbound webhook delivery), Moberg.Warp.Worker, Moberg.Warp.UI, and Moberg.Warp.Http (optional). Observability add-ons: Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Http and Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Refit (observe outbound calls the app makes to other services). A provider package — Moberg.Warp.Provider.PostgreSql or Moberg.Warp.Provider.SqlServer — is required: it supplies `opt.UsePostgreSql()` / `opt.UseSqlServer()` and the row-locking / DB-push SQL specific to that engine.

---

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Core              # Publishing (required)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Provider.PostgreSql  # or Moberg.Warp.Provider.SqlServer (required)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Worker            # Worker service (if processing jobs)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.UI                # Dashboard (optional)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Http              # HTTP exposure for IRequest<T> / IStreamRequest<T> + inbound observability (optional)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Http     # Observe outbound HttpClient calls (optional)
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Refit    # Refit operation-name sugar for adapters (optional)
```

---

## Setup

### 1. Register DbContext

Register your DbContext normally. Warp hooks into it automatically:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(options =>
    options.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default")));
```

### 2. Register Warp

Handlers (`IJobHandler<>`, `IMessageHandler<>`, `IRequestHandler<,>`) and pipeline behaviors (`IPipelineBehavior<,>`) are discovered by Warp's source generator at compile time — there are no `AddJobHandlers(asm)` / `AddPipelineBehaviors(asm)` extension methods. The source generator emits a `[ModuleInitializer]` per assembly that registers all discovered handlers into a public registry, which `AddWarp` / `AddWarpServer` replays onto your `IServiceCollection`. Define a handler class, build, and it's wired.

For publisher-only apps (create jobs but don't process them):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarp<AppDbContext>(opt => opt.UsePostgreSql());
```

For worker apps (create AND process jobs):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();   // required — provider opt-in
    opt.WorkerCount = 10;
    opt.Queues = ["default"];
    opt.PollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);
});
```

`AddWarpServer` includes `AddWarp` internally — don't call both. `opt.UsePostgreSql()` (or `opt.UseSqlServer()`) **must** be called inside the lambda so the provider package's row-locking and DB-push wiring takes effect.

> **Multi-project solutions.** The source generator scans handlers transitively across project references and registers them all into the host. If a host references an assembly whose handlers it doesn't want in its DI graph (e.g., an API host that pulls in worker-only handlers via a Domain → Worker → Domain chain), opt that assembly out: `opt.ExcludeHandlersFromAssembly(typeof(WorkerOnlyMarker).Assembly)`. See the Multi-Project Source Generation page for the full picture.

### 3. Create Database Schema

Warp entities are added to your DbContext model automatically. Use standard EF Core migrations:

```bash
dotnet ef migrations add AddWarp
dotnet ef database update
```

> **DbContext must be registered via `AddDbContext<TContext>(...)`**, not `AddDbContextFactory<TContext>(...)` alone. The factory overload registers `IDbContextFactory<TContext>` but not `TContext`, so Warp's scoped services can't resolve it — `AddWarp` will throw at startup. If your app uses the factory pattern (Blazor, etc.), call both. For design-time tooling (`dotnet ef migrations`) the migrations project must use a real `Host.CreateApplicationBuilder` that calls `AddDbContext` — otherwise EF design-time skips Warp's `IModelCustomizer` and produces an empty migration.
>
> **All addon entities are registered unconditionally.** Whether or not your host calls `opt.AddConcurrency()` / `AddCircuitBreaker()` / `AddRateLimit()` / `AddSagas()`, the corresponding tables (`warp.concurrency_limit`, `warp.circuit_breaker_state`, `warp.rate_limit_bucket`, `warp.rate_limit_override`, `warp.saga_state`, `warp.saga_job_link`) are in the schema. One migration covers every deployment shape — no need to mirror addon opt-ins between your API host, Workers host, and migrations host. The opt-in methods still gate the runtime behavior (pipeline behaviors, admin services); the schema is just always there. See the EF Core Integration page for the full picture.

When upgrading the Warp NuGet package:

```bash
dotnet ef migrations add UpgradeWarp
dotnet ef database update
```

For quick start/development only (does not support upgrades):

```csharp
await context.Database.EnsureCreatedAsync();
```

### 4. Add Dashboard (Optional)

```csharp
app.MapWarpUI("/warp"); // Serves at /warp
```

### 5. Complete Minimal Example

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(options =>
    options.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default")));

builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();   // provider opt-in (required)
    opt.WorkerCount = 5;
    opt.Queues = ["default"];
});

var app = builder.Build();

app.MapWarpUI("/warp");
app.Run();
```

---

## Three Patterns

### Type Hierarchy

All types implement `IRequest<TResponse>`:

```csharp
public interface IRequest<out TResponse>;     // Base — all types implement this
public interface IJob : IRequest<Unit>;        // Persistent, single handler
public interface IMessage : IRequest<Unit>;    // Persistent, multiple handlers
// IRequest<TResponse> used directly           // In-memory, returns TResponse
```

| Pattern | Interface | Persistence | Handlers | Response | Dispatch |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------|----------|
| Messages | `IMessage` | Database | Multiple | Unit | `publisher.Publish()` |
| Jobs | `IJob` | Database | Single | Unit | `publisher.Enqueue()` / `Schedule()` |
| Requests | `IRequest<T>` | In-memory | Single | Typed `T` | `mediator.Send()` |

---

## Pattern 1: Messages (Pub/Sub)

Messages implement `IMessage` and have multiple handlers. Each handler becomes an independent, retryable job.

### Define a message and handlers

```csharp
public class OrderPlaced : IMessage
{
    public int OrderId { get; set; }
}

public class SendConfirmationEmail : IMessageHandler<OrderPlaced>
{
    private readonly ILogger<SendConfirmationEmail> _logger;

    public SendConfirmationEmail(ILogger<SendConfirmationEmail> logger) => _logger = logger;

    public async Task HandleAsync(OrderPlaced message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        _logger.LogInformation("Sending email for order {OrderId}", message.OrderId);
        // ILogger output is captured and viewable in the dashboard
    }
}

public class NotifyWarehouse : IMessageHandler<OrderPlaced>
{
    public async Task HandleAsync(OrderPlaced message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        // Runs independently — if email handler fails, this still succeeds
    }
}
```

### Publish

```csharp
await publisher.Publish(new OrderPlaced { OrderId = 123 });
await context.SaveChangesAsync(); // Committed atomically with business data
```

### How message routing works

1. `Publish()` creates a `Job` entity with `Kind = Message` in the database
2. `MessageRouter` (background task, polls every 1s) discovers all registered `IMessageHandler<T>` implementations
3. For each handler, a child `Job` is created with `Kind = Job` and the handler pre-assigned
4. Workers pick up each child job independently
5. When all children complete, the parent message transitions to `Completed` or `Failed`

---

## Pattern 2: Jobs (Background Work)

Jobs implement `IJob` and have a single handler. They support scheduling, retries, continuations, batches, named queues, and mutex.

### Define a job and handler

```csharp
public class GenerateReport : IJob
{
    public int ReportId { get; set; }
}

public class GenerateReportHandler : IJobHandler<GenerateReport>
{
    private readonly ILogger<GenerateReportHandler> _logger;

    public GenerateReportHandler(ILogger<GenerateReportHandler> logger) => _logger = logger;

    public async Task HandleAsync(GenerateReport message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        _logger.LogInformation("Generating report {ReportId}", message.ReportId);
        // Handler logs appear in the job's Activity Log on the dashboard
    }
}
```

### Enqueue

```csharp
await publisher.Enqueue(new GenerateReport { ReportId = 1 });
await publisher.SaveChangesAsync();
```

### Schedule for later

```csharp
await publisher.Schedule(new GenerateReport { ReportId = 1 }, DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(1));
await publisher.SaveChangesAsync();
```

### Retries

Declare retry policy on the handler or job class:

```csharp
[Retry(3, Delays = [15, 60, 300])]
public class GenerateReportHandler : IJobHandler<GenerateReport> { ... }
```

Or configure global defaults via the builder lambda:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();
    opt.AddRetry(o => { o.MaxRetries = 3; o.Delays = [15, 60, 300]; o.JitterFactor = 0.2; });
});
```

All addon opt-ins (`AddRetry`, `AddTimeout`, `AddConcurrency`, `AddCircuitBreaker`, `AddRateLimit`, `AddNoRestart`, `AddSagas`, `UseDatabasePush`, `AddDashboardPush`) are extension methods on the `IWarpBuilder<TContext>` lambda parameter (`opt`), not service-collection extensions.

Priority: per-enqueue metadata > handler attribute > job attribute > global RetryOptions. Failed jobs are retried automatically. Crash requeues do NOT count against the retry limit.

`JitterFactor` (global only, default `0.0`, clamped to `[0, 1]`) applies multiplicative random jitter to each computed delay: `delay * (1 + JitterFactor * rand(-1, 1))`. Spreads retries to avoid thundering herds when many jobs fail at the same time.

### Named queues

```csharp
await publisher.Enqueue(new GenerateReport { ReportId = 1 }, queue: "reports");
```

Queues are processed in alphabetical order. Use prefixes to control priority:

```csharp
options.Queues = ["a-critical", "b-default", "c-low"];
// Workers always pick from a-critical before b-default, etc.
```

### Continuations

```csharp
var parentId = await publisher.Enqueue(new ProcessPayment { OrderId = 1 });
await publisher.Enqueue(new SendReceipt { OrderId = 1 }, parentId); // Runs after parent completes
await publisher.SaveChangesAsync();
```

### Batches

```csharp
var batchPublisher = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IBatchPublisher>();

var jobs = orders.Select(o => new ProcessOrder { OrderId = o.Id }).ToList();
var batchId = await batchPublisher.StartNew(jobs);
await batchPublisher.SaveChangesAsync();

// Continuation after batch completes
var followUps = new List<SendSummary> { new() };
await batchPublisher.ContinueBatchWith(followUps, batchId);
await batchPublisher.SaveChangesAsync();
```

#### ContinuationOptions

```csharp
// Default: continuation fires only when ALL jobs succeed
await batchPublisher.StartNew(jobs, options: ContinuationOptions.OnlyOnSucceeded);

// Fire when all jobs finish, regardless of success/failure
await batchPublisher.StartNew(jobs, options: ContinuationOptions.OnAnyFinishedState);
```

With `OnlyOnSucceeded` (default): if any job fails, the batch transitions to `Failed` and continuations stay in `Awaiting` state. You can requeue failed jobs from the dashboard.

With `OnAnyFinishedState`: continuations fire as soon as all jobs reach a terminal state.

### Mutex (concurrency control)

Only one job per mutex key can be processing at a time:

```csharp
await publisher.Enqueue(
    new ProcessPayment { CustomerId = 123 },
    new JobParameters { Mutex = "payment:123" });
```

If a worker picks up a job whose mutex is already held by another processing job, the new job is cancelled automatically. Jobs without a mutex skip the check entirely (zero overhead).

### NoRestart (stale-recovery opt-out)

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddNoRestart()` on the `AddWarp`/`AddWarpServer` builder. Lets specific job types stay `Failed` on worker crash instead of being auto-requeued by `StaleJobRecovery`.

```csharp
[NoRestart]
public class ChargeCard : IJob { }
```

Override chain (first non-null wins): per-publish `.WithRestart(bool)` > `[NoRestart]`/`[Restart]` attribute (inherits through base classes, with direct-declaration precedence) > global `RestartStaleJobsByDefault` (default `true`). Use for non-idempotent work: payments, webhooks, outbound notifications.

### Circuit Breaker

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddCircuitBreaker(o => ...)` on the `AddWarp`/`AddWarpServer` builder. The `CircuitBreakerState` entity is part of Warp's base schema (registered unconditionally), so no separate migration is required when you turn the addon on. Opens after `Threshold` consecutive failures, stays open for `Duration`, then transitions to **HalfOpen** where an atomic CAS guarantees exactly one worker probes while others reschedule.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();
    opt.AddCircuitBreaker(o =>
    {
        o.Threshold = 5;
        o.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
        o.ResetJitter = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
    });
});

[CircuitBreaker(Group = "payments-gateway")]
public class ChargeCard : IJob { }
```

Jobs rescheduled by an open circuit do NOT increment Retry's `RetriedTimes` — the retry budget is preserved for when the circuit closes.

### Batched Completions (Dispatcher Mode)

When `UseDispatcher = true`, each worker buffers job completions and commits them as a single multi-row transaction. Tune via `CompletionBatchSize` (default `50`) and `CompletionFlushInterval` (default `100ms`). Set `CompletionBatchSize = 1` to opt out.

Poison-entry isolation: a single bad row in a batch of 50 is dropped via recursive split, the other 49 still commit. SIGTERM mid-flush is safe — `FlushAsync()` commits to completion using `CancellationToken.None` internally. Trade-off: at-least-once semantics. Pair with `[NoRestart]` for non-idempotent handlers.

### JobParameters

For full control, pass a `JobParameters` object:

```csharp
await publisher.Enqueue(new MyJob(), new JobParameters
{
    MaxRetries = 3,
    Queue = "critical",
    Mutex = "my-resource-key",
    ScheduleTime = DateTime.UtcNow.AddMinutes(30),
    ParentId = parentJobId,  // continuation
});
```

---

## Pattern 3: Requests (In-Memory Mediator)

Requests implement `IRequest<TResponse>` and execute immediately in-process. No database, no worker, no retries.

### Define a request and handler

```csharp
public class GetUser : IRequest<UserDto>
{
    public int UserId { get; set; }
}

public class GetUserHandler : IRequestHandler<GetUser, UserDto>
{
    private readonly AppDbContext _db;

    public GetUserHandler(AppDbContext db) => _db = db;

    public async Task<UserDto> HandleAsync(GetUser request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var user = await _db.Users.FindAsync(request.UserId, ct);
        return new UserDto { Id = user.Id, Name = user.Name };
    }
}
```

### Send via IMediator

```csharp
public class UserController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;

    public async Task<IActionResult> GetUser(int id)
    {
        var user = await _mediator.Send(new GetUser { UserId = id });
        return Ok(user);
    }
}
```

### Key differences from Jobs/Messages

- Requests are NOT persisted to the database
- They execute immediately in-process, returning `TResponse` directly
- Errors bubble up to the caller (no automatic retries)
- Not visible in the dashboard
- Use `IMediator.Send()`, not `IPublisher.Enqueue()`

---

## Transactional Outbox Pattern

Jobs are created inside the same database transaction as your business data. A single `SaveChangesAsync()` commits everything atomically.

```csharp
public async Task<IActionResult> PlaceOrder(CreateOrderRequest request)
{
    var order = new Order { CustomerId = request.CustomerId };
    _context.Orders.Add(order);

    // These jobs are written to the same DbContext — not yet committed
    await _publisher.Enqueue(new SendConfirmationEmail { OrderId = order.Id });
    await _publisher.Publish(new OrderPlaced { OrderId = order.Id });

    // Single SaveChangesAsync commits the order AND all jobs atomically
    await _context.SaveChangesAsync();
    return Ok(order.Id);
}
```

If `SaveChangesAsync()` fails, both the order and the jobs roll back. No orphaned jobs.

### DbContext must be Scoped

The publisher and your application code must share the same DbContext instance. Register your DbContext as Scoped (the EF Core default). Do NOT use Transient lifetime.

### With explicit transactions

```csharp
await using var transaction = await context.Database.BeginTransactionAsync();

context.Orders.Add(order);
await publisher.Enqueue(new ProcessOrder { OrderId = order.Id });

await context.SaveChangesAsync();
await transaction.CommitAsync(); // Jobs visible to workers only after commit
```

---

## Pipeline Behaviors

A unified pipeline wraps all handler invocations — jobs, messages, and requests. Implement `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` for cross-cutting concerns:

```csharp
public class LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
{
    private readonly ILogger<LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>> _logger;

    public LoggingBehavior(ILogger<LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>> logger) => _logger = logger;

    public async Task<TResponse> HandleAsync(
        TRequest request,
        RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next,
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        _logger.LogInformation("Handling {RequestType}", typeof(TRequest).Name);
        var response = await next();
        _logger.LogInformation("Handled {RequestType}", typeof(TRequest).Name);
        return response;
    }
}
```

### Registration

Pipeline behaviors are picked up by the same source generator that wires handlers — no `AddPipelineBehaviors(asm)` call needed. Define a class implementing `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>`, build, and it's registered. For an open-generic behavior, the generator emits a single `services.AddTransient(typeof(IPipelineBehavior<,>), typeof(LoggingBehavior<,>))`.

### Targeting specific types

```csharp
// Only for GetUser requests
public class CacheBehavior : IPipelineBehavior<GetUser, UserDto> { ... }

// Only for jobs (any IJob) — TResponse is Unit for IJob/IMessage
public class RetryBehavior<T> : IPipelineBehavior<T, Unit> where T : IJob { ... }
```

`IPipelineBehavior<,>` runs on all three dispatch paths: `IMediator.Send` (for `IRequest<>`), the worker's job-execution loop (for `IJob`, with `TResponse = Unit`), and the message-routing path (for `IMessage`, with `TResponse = Unit`). Each path uses its own behavior chain — registering an open-generic `IPipelineBehavior<,>` binds it to all of them. Behaviors execute in registration order, outermost first.

### Short-circuiting from a behavior

To override the default outcome (e.g., refuse retry, mark as deleted), construct a new `JobOutcome` and assign it to `IJobContext.Outcome` — `JobOutcome` is init-only by design, so you cannot mutate an existing instance:

```csharp
public class RefuseRetryBehavior<T> : IPipelineBehavior<T, Unit> where T : IJob
{
    private readonly IJobContext _jobContext;

    public RefuseRetryBehavior(IJobContext jobContext) => _jobContext = jobContext;

    public async Task<Unit> HandleAsync(T request, RequestHandlerDelegate<Unit> next, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try { return await next(); }
        catch (DomainRefusedException)
        {
            _jobContext.Outcome = new JobOutcome
            {
                State = State.Failed,
                LogMessage = "Short-circuited: domain refused this work",
            };
            throw;
        }
    }
}
```

---

## Recurring Jobs

Register a cron-based recurring job:

```csharp
var recurringPublisher = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IRecurringJobPublisher>();

await recurringPublisher.AddOrUpdateRecurringJob(
    new CleanupSessions(),
    name: "session-cleanup",
    cron: "0 * * * *");  // Every hour
```

`AddOrUpdateRecurringJob` only registers the definition — it does NOT create a job. The `RecurringJobScheduler` background task creates jobs when the cron time arrives.

### Cron expressions

Standard 5-part (minute, hour, day, month, weekday) and 6-part with seconds:

```
* * * * *       Every minute
0 * * * *       Every hour
0 9 * * *       Daily at 9 AM
0 0 * * 1       Every Monday at midnight
*/5 * * * *     Every 5 minutes
0 9 * * 1-5     Weekdays at 9 AM
```

### Update

Call `AddOrUpdateRecurringJob` again with the same name:

```csharp
await recurringPublisher.AddOrUpdateRecurringJob(
    new CleanupSessions(),
    name: "session-cleanup",
    cron: "*/30 * * * *");  // Changed to every 30 minutes
```

### Manual trigger

Every single-definition method on `IRecurringJobService` keys on the registered NAME (not the table's surrogate id): `TriggerRecurringJob`, `EnableRecurringJob`, `DisableRecurringJob`, `DeleteRecurringJob`, `GetRecurringJob`, `GetRecurringJobHistory`. Names are trimmed, must be non-empty, and are capped at 200 characters. An unknown name throws `ArgumentException`.

```csharp
var svc = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IRecurringJobService>();
await svc.TriggerRecurringJob("session-cleanup");
```

The trigger stages one extra job at `ScheduleTime = now` and fires the JobEnqueued wake; the cron schedule and `NextExecution` are untouched. An explicit trigger ignores `DisabledAt` (operator override).

### Delete

```csharp
await recurringJobService.DeleteRecurringJob("session-cleanup");
```

### Deduplication

Before creating a new job, the scheduler checks if the most recent execution is still Enqueued or Processing. If so, it skips — no duplicate jobs.

---

## Job Cancellation

Warp uses graceful cancellation. When you cancel a processing job, the handler gets a chance to stop cleanly.

### Cancel a job

```csharp
await jobCommandService.DeleteJob(jobId);
```

### Flow

1. `DeleteJob` sets `CancellationMode = Graceful` (state stays `Processing`)
2. `RunJobMonitor` detects it and cancels the handler's `CancellationToken`
3. If handler respects the token: state becomes `Deleted`
4. If handler completes despite cancellation: state becomes `Completed` (work happened)

`CancelBatch(batchId)` cancels a whole batch (surfaced as a Cancel action on the batch detail page). It walks the `ParentJobId` tree breadth-first and gracefully cancels every non-terminal descendant — direct children plus pending continuations reached through already-finished children — leaving terminal jobs (`Completed`/`Failed`/`Deleted`) untouched.

### Writing cancellable handlers

```csharp
public class LongRunningHandler : IJobHandler<LongRunningJob>
{
    public async Task HandleAsync(LongRunningJob message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        foreach (var item in items)
        {
            ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
            await ProcessItem(item);
        }
    }
}
```

---

## Crash Recovery

Warp uses a sliding invisibility timeout to detect and recover from worker crashes.

1. When a worker picks up a job, it sets `LastKeepAlive = now`
2. During execution, keep-alive is refreshed every `InvisibilityTimeout / 5` (default: every 60s with a 5-minute timeout)
3. If the worker crashes, the keep-alive stops
4. After `InvisibilityTimeout` (default 5 minutes), the job is requeued automatically
5. Crash requeues do NOT count against `MaxRetries`

---

## Job Tracing

Every job gets two trace fields:

- `TraceId` — All related jobs share this ID. The first job creates it.
- `SpawnedByJobId` — Direct "who created me" link.

When a handler creates new jobs, they automatically inherit the trace via `AsyncLocal` context:

```csharp
public class ProcessOrderHandler : IJobHandler<ProcessOrder>
{
    private readonly IBatchPublisher _batchPublisher;

    public async Task HandleAsync(ProcessOrder message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        // These jobs automatically inherit the trace from ProcessOrder
        var items = orders.Select(i => new ShipItem { ItemId = i.Id }).ToList();
        await _batchPublisher.StartNew(items);
    }
}
```

---

## Job Metadata

Attach key-value metadata to jobs at publish time. Metadata is inherited by child jobs, accessible in handlers via `IJobContext`, and visible in the dashboard.

### Ad-hoc metadata

```csharp
await publisher.Enqueue(new ProcessOrder { OrderId = 123 }, new JobParameters
{
    Metadata = new Dictionary<string, string>
    {
        ["tenant"] = "acme-corp",
        ["priority"] = "high",
    },
});
```

### Reading metadata in handlers

```csharp
public class ProcessOrderHandler : IJobHandler<ProcessOrder>
{
    private readonly IJobContext _jobContext;

    public ProcessOrderHandler(IJobContext jobContext) => _jobContext = jobContext;

    public async Task HandleAsync(ProcessOrder message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var tenant = _jobContext.Metadata["tenant"];
        var jobId = _jobContext.JobId;
        var traceId = _jobContext.TraceId;
    }
}
```

### Publish pipeline behaviors

For cross-cutting metadata (e.g., tenant ID on every job), implement `IPublishPipelineBehavior<T>`:

```csharp
public class TenantMetadataBehavior<T> : IPublishPipelineBehavior<T>
{
    private readonly ITenantProvider _tenantProvider;

    public TenantMetadataBehavior(ITenantProvider tenantProvider) => _tenantProvider = tenantProvider;

    public async Task PublishAsync(PublishContext<T> context, PublishDelegate next, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        context.Metadata["tenant"] = _tenantProvider.CurrentTenantId;
        await next();
    }
}

// Register as open generic
builder.Services.AddTransient(typeof(IPublishPipelineBehavior<>), typeof(TenantMetadataBehavior<>));
```

### Metadata inheritance

When a handler creates child jobs, metadata from the parent is automatically inherited. Ad-hoc metadata from `JobParameters` merges with inherited metadata (ad-hoc wins on key conflict).

### Metadata sources (priority order)

1. Inherited metadata — from parent job's execution context
2. Ad-hoc metadata — from `JobParameters.Metadata`
3. Pipeline metadata — from `IPublishPipelineBehavior<T>` implementations

Later sources override earlier ones for the same key.

---

## Pause / Resume

Pause and resume job processing at the server or worker group level.

### API

```
POST /api/servers/{serverId}/pause
POST /api/servers/{serverId}/resume
POST /api/groups/{groupId}/pause
POST /api/groups/{groupId}/resume
```

### How it works

1. Pause request sets `PausedAt` timestamp on the server or worker group
2. `Heartbeat` task (every ~3s) reads pause state from database into `PauseStateHolder`
3. Workers check `PauseStateHolder` before each poll — if paused, skip
4. Resume clears `PausedAt`, next heartbeat propagates the change

Paused workers stop picking up new jobs. Jobs already in progress continue to completion.

---

## Real-time Handler Logs

Handler `ILogger` output is flushed to the database every ~1 second during execution (not just after completion). Logs are visible in the dashboard while the job is still processing.

The `RunJobMonitor` task runs alongside each handler execution, periodically draining the log collector and persisting entries. This also handles keep-alive updates and cancellation detection.

---

## Concurrency Control: Mutex & Semaphore

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddConcurrency()`. One primitive (`IWarpSemaphoreProvider`, Medallion distributed locks), two attributes. At most N jobs per key run at any moment across all workers/servers. Zero overhead for jobs without a key.

- `[Mutex("key")]` — limit fixed at 1, default `ConcurrencyMode.Skip`. Also `.WithMutex("key", mode?)` on `JobParameters`.
- `[Semaphore("key", limit: N)]` — N slots, default `ConcurrencyMode.Wait`. Also `.WithSemaphore("key", limit, mode?)`.
- `ConcurrencyMode` (from 1): `Skip` → surplus short-circuited to `Deleted`; `Wait` → surplus requeued (`Enqueued`, `ScheduleTime = now`).
- Lock is held for the **whole handler execution** (contrast rate limit). Lock name `warp:concurrency:{key}`.
- Admin overrides via `IConcurrencyLimitManager.AddOrUpdateLimit/RemoveLimit` (entity `ConcurrencyLimit`). Precedence: admin row > attribute/extension limit > 1. Admin rows are sticky across deploys.
- Namespaces are disjoint by design: `[Mutex("k")]` uses `warp:concurrency:k`; `[Semaphore("k", N)]` uses `warp:concurrency:k:0..k:{N-1}`. Don't put both on the same key.
- Dashboard `/warp/concurrency` (hide-on-404 nav).

## Job Timeout

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddTimeout(o => { o.Default; o.DefaultMode; o.DefaultScope; })` (`Default = null` = unrestricted). Caps handler run time; on deadline the handler's `CancellationToken` is cancelled (cooperative only — a handler that ignores the token runs to `Completed`).

- `[Timeout(seconds: N, Mode =, Scope =)]` or `.WithTimeout(TimeSpan)` (per-publish wins).
- `TimeoutMode` (from 1): `Delete` (default) → `Deleted`, **not** retried by `AddRetry`; `Fail` → throws `TimeoutException`, **caught** by `AddRetry`.
- `TimeoutScope` (from 1): `PerAttempt` (default) → fresh budget per retry; `Total` → `DeadlineUtc` stamped at publish, bounds the whole chain (only useful with `Fail`).
- **Ordering: `AddRetry()` before `AddTimeout()`** (DI order = outer → inner; retry must wrap timeout to catch its `TimeoutException`).

## Rate Limit

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddRateLimit()`. Throttles jobs sharing a key to N starts per window.

- `[RateLimit("key", count: N, perSeconds: S, Mode =, Style =)]` or `.WithRateLimit("key", count, window)`.
- `RateLimitMode` (from 1): `Skip` (default) → `Deleted`; `Wait` → rescheduled via `JobOutcome.RescheduledState` (100–500 ms jitter).
- `RateLimitStyle` (from 1): `Fixed` (default) → wall-clock window floor-aligned to UTC ticks; `Sliding` → rolling window over last N starts; `TokenBucket` → paces (not caps): tokens refill continuously at `count/perSeconds`/s up to a burst of `count`, `Wait`-mode reschedules to the next token-refill instant so a backlog trickles at the steady rate.
- `perSeconds` capped at 7 days. Live state in `RateLimitBucket`. Lock held only for the brief check-and-increment (**not** during handler execution, unlike Mutex).
- Admin overrides via `IRateLimitOverrideManager`; precedence admin row > attribute > publish-time. Dashboard `/warp/ratelimits`.
- **Ordering: `AddConcurrency()` before `AddRateLimit()`** so a mutex rejection doesn't waste a token. DB push does **not** accelerate `Wait` reschedules (they ride `ScheduledJobActivation`).

## Circuit Breaker

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddCircuitBreaker(o => { o.Threshold = 3; o.Duration = 1m; o.ResetJitter = 10s; })`. `CircuitBreakerState` entity is in the base schema.

- `[CircuitBreaker(Group =, Threshold =, DurationSeconds =, ResetJitterSeconds =)]`. Default key = `typeof(TRequest).Name`; `Group` shares one circuit across handlers.
- Three states: `Closed` (runs; failure count resets on success, opens at `Threshold` consecutive failures) → `Open` (`OpenUntil > now`; jobs rescheduled to `OpenUntil + jitter` without running) → `HalfOpen` (one worker wins a CAS probe; success → Closed, failure → Open).
- Short-circuits **before** Retry — a job blocked by an open circuit does not increment `RetriedTimes` (retry budget preserved). Runs after the concurrency behavior.

## No-Restart (Stale-Recovery Opt-Out)

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddNoRestart()`. Controls whether a job requeues or fails when a worker crashes mid-execution (independent of Retry, which governs handler throws).

- `[NoRestart]` (never requeue on crash → `Failed`), `[Restart]` (opt back in), or `.WithRestart(bool)` (per-publish, wins). Both attributes inherit through base classes (closest declaration wins); applying both to one class throws.
- Global default `RestartStaleJobsByDefault` on `WarpServerConfiguration` (default `true`).
- Override chain (first non-null wins): `.WithRestart()` > attribute > global default. `StaleJobRecovery` resolves it: `false` → `Failed` (`ExpireAt = null`, never auto-deleted); `true` → `Enqueued`.
- Use for non-idempotent work (payments, outbound notifications, non-idempotent APIs). `.WithRestart(bool)` works even without the addon; the attributes need it.

## Batched Completions (Dispatcher Mode)

Automatic when `UseDispatcher = true` — each `WarpDispatcherWorker` buffers job completions and flushes them as one multi-row transaction, collapsing N commits into one.

- `CompletionBatchSize` (default 50), `CompletionFlushInterval` (default 100 ms). Set `CompletionBatchSize = 1` to opt out (immediate flush).
- Poison-entry isolation: a failing batch splits in half recursively; a single bad row is dropped, the rest commit. `StaleJobRecovery` handles orphaned `Processing` rows.
- At-least-once: a crash between handler completion and flush leaves the job `Processing` → recovered per `CanBeRestarted`. Pair non-idempotent handlers with `[NoRestart]`. Throughput optimization, not latency.

## Sagas

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddSagas()`; register handlers with `services.AddSagaHandler<TSagaHandler>()`. In `Warp.Core.Sagas`. Adds entities `SagaState` (one row per live saga, deleted on completion) + `SagaJobLink` (activity log, FK cascade).

- State class: subclass `Saga` (or `Saga<TKey>` for typed `string`/`Guid`/`int`/`long` keys).
- Messages: carry exactly one `[Correlate]` property (`string`/`Guid`/`int`/`long`, canonicalized to one `varchar(200)`); mark saga-starting messages `[StartsSaga]`.
- Handler: implement `ISagaHandler<TSaga, TMessage>` per message type. Call `saga.MarkCompleted()` to delete the row in the same `SaveChanges` (key immediately reusable).
- Proxy serializes per correlation key on `warp:saga:{TSaga.FullName}:{key}` via `IWarpSemaphoreProvider`; optimistic `Version` concurrency. `SagaPiiCheck` blocks PII-named `[Correlate]` props at registration (opt out with `[Correlate(IsAnonymized = true)]`). `ISagaCommandService.ForceComplete`. Dashboard `/warp/sagas`.

## Background Services

Base feature (no addon opt-in for the schema — `AddWarp<TContext>` always adds the four entities `Definition`/`Instance`/`Lease`/`Log` and `IBackgroundServiceQueryService`). Register services with `opt.AddBackgroundService<T>()`; `AddWarpServer` adds the host. In `Warp.Core.BackgroundServices`.

- Subclass `WarpBackgroundService`; override `Scope` → `ServiceScope.PerServer` (default, one instance per server) or `ServiceScope.Singleton` (one active cluster-wide, coordinated via `BackgroundServiceLease` 30 s TTL renewed in `Heartbeat`; ~30 s failover on hard-kill / ~0 s on graceful shutdown).
- Subclasses are **singletons** — inject `IServiceScopeFactory`, never `DbContext` (`ValidateScopes = true` catches the captive-dependency foot-gun at startup).
- `opt.DisableWorker()` → service-only server (background services + `Heartbeat`/`ServerCleanup`/`ExpirationCleanup`, no job worker or job tasks; provider still required).
- Log capture auto-wired (`MinLogLevel` default Information, 100/s cap, 4 KB truncation, 1000-row/7-day retention). Dashboard `/warp/services`.

## Database Push

Opt-in addon: call the provider first, then `opt.UseDatabasePush()`. Replaces polling wake-up with PostgreSQL `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY` or SQL Server Service Broker.

- Accelerates (< 50 ms): dispatcher fetch (`JobEnqueued`, only when `UseDispatcher = true`), `MessageRouter` (`MessageEnqueued`), `Orchestrator` (`JobFinalized`). Individual-worker mode keeps polling (thundering-herd avoidance).
- In-process every `WarpWorker` already shortcuts backoff on a same-server `JobEnqueued` signal regardless of push. Scheduled jobs are still bounded by `ScheduledActivationInterval` (default 5 s) — push accelerates only what happens after activation.
- Transports never throw from publish (log + `warp.notifications.publish_failures`); missed notifications caught by drain-on-reconnect. SQL Server requires `ALTER DATABASE ... SET ENABLE_BROKER` (degrades to polling with an actionable log otherwise).

## Dashboard Push

Opt-in addon: `opt.AddDashboardPush(o => o.CoalesceWindow = 100ms)`. SignalR hub at `${RoutePrefix}/api/hub`; broadcasts `JobFinalized` / `MessageEnqueued` events carrying a `DashboardStatistics` snapshot. Without it the dashboard runs on REST refetch + a 30 s safety-net poll.

- The broadcaster is the third consumer of `ServerTaskSignals<TContext>` (after `Orchestrator` and `MessageRouter`). Per-view data (job lists, detail, logs) stays on event-driven REST refetch.
- Multi-server fanout requires `opt.UseDatabasePush()` (single-server works without it). Frontend reads `${RoutePrefix}/api/addons` once at boot and connects only when `push: true`.

## Database-Generated IDs (outbox gotcha)

`publisher.Enqueue`/`Publish` serialize the message payload to JSON **immediately** (writing the `Job` row into the change tracker), before `SaveChangesAsync` populates a DB-generated identity — so a payload capturing `entity.Id` freezes `0`. Three fixes, all preserving the outbox guarantee:

1. **Client-assigned `Guid` PK** (recommended for new schemas) — assign `Id = Guid.NewGuid()` before `Add`; one save. Use Guid v7 if insertion order matters.
2. **EF Core Hi/Lo** (`modelBuilder.Entity<T>().Property(x => x.Id).UseHiLo()`) — client-side id block, keeps integer PKs; one save; gaps after restarts.
3. **Two `SaveChanges` in one explicit transaction** — save the entity to populate its id, then enqueue; works on legacy schemas, extra round-trip.

---

## Configuration Reference

### Core Configuration (AddWarp)

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarp<AppDbContext>(options =>
{
    options.Schema = "warp";                                  // Database schema (default: "warp", null for default)
    options.DefaultQueue = "default";                          // Default queue name (default: "default")
    options.JobExpirationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromDays(1);       // Completed/deleted job retention (default: 1 day)
});
```

### Worker Configuration (AddWarpServer)

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(options =>
{
    // Worker
    options.WorkerCount = 10;                                  // Concurrent workers (default: min(CPU*5, 20))
    options.PollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);         // Poll delay when idle; also floor for backoff (default: 1s)
    options.MaxPollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);     // Ceiling for exponential backoff (default: 30s)
    options.PollingIntervalFactor = 2.0;                       // Multiplier per empty poll; 1.0 disables backoff (default: 2.0)
    options.Queues = ["a-critical", "b-default", "c-low"];     // Subscribed queues (default: ["default"])

    // Handler logging
    options.EnableHandlerLogging = true;                       // false to suppress ILogger capture (default: true)
    options.LogFlushInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);        // How often handler logs drain to DB (default: 1s)

    // Dispatcher mode (batch-fetch instead of per-worker polling)
    options.UseDispatcher = false;                             // default: false
    options.CompletionBatchSize = 50;                          // Dispatcher only. Max completions per flush (default: 50)
    options.CompletionFlushInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100); // Dispatcher only (default: 100ms)
    // Stale recovery opt-out default — with NoRestart addon and [NoRestart]/[Restart] attributes, flip per-type
    options.RestartStaleJobsByDefault = true;                  // false makes stale jobs Failed by default (default: true)

    // Cancellation
    options.CancellationCheckInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5); // default: 5s

    // Server identity
    options.ServerName = "my-api-server";                      // Dashboard display name
    options.ServerId = Guid.NewGuid();                          // Auto-generated

    // Health & crash recovery
    options.HealthCheckInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);    // default: 10s
    options.HealthCheckTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);      // Server considered dead after this (default: 5m)
    options.InvisibilityTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);     // Stale job requeue threshold (default: 5m)

    // Job retention
    options.JobExpirationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromDays(1);       // default: 1 day
    options.ExpirationBatchSize = 1000;                        // default: 1000
    options.MaxExpirableJobCount = null;                        // null = unlimited (default: null)

    // Background task intervals
    options.OrchestrationInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
    options.MessageRoutingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);
    options.CounterAggregationInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);
    options.ServerCleanupInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
    options.StaleJobRecoveryInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
    options.ExpirationCleanupInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60);

    // Inherited from WarpConfiguration
    options.DefaultQueue = "default";
});
```

### Worker Groups

Split workers into groups with independent queues and polling intervals:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(options =>
{
    // Top-level settings become the first worker group
    options.WorkerCount = 5;
    options.Queues = ["critical"];
    options.PollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100);

    // Additional group
    options.AddWorkerGroup(group =>
    {
        group.WorkerCount = 2;
        group.Queues = ["reports", "default"];
        group.PollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);
        group.MaxPollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60);   // per-group ceiling
        group.PollingIntervalFactor = 2.0;                      // per-group multiplier
    });
});
// Creates 7 workers total: 5 on "critical" @ 100ms, 2 on "reports"/"default" @ 5s
// On idle queues, each group backs off geometrically: floor → floor*factor → … → MaxPollingInterval.
// Any processed job resets the delay to the floor instantly.
```

### Dashboard Configuration

```csharp
app.MapWarpUI("/warp").RequireAuthorization("WarpDashboard");
```

---

## Dashboard Authorization

The dashboard is a set of routed ASP.NET Core endpoints. `MapWarpUI` returns an endpoint builder covering
the SPA shell, the REST API and the SignalR hub, so one convention gates all three. Default (no
convention) is open access. Because ASP.NET makes the decision, an anonymous caller is CHALLENGED (reaches
your sign-in) while an authenticated caller lacking the permission is FORBIDDEN (403 / AccessDeniedPath) —
and authorization requirements are async, so a DB-backed permission check is an ordinary await.

### Gate on your own policy (host has an identity system)

Needs nothing from Warp:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAuthorizationBuilder()
    .AddPolicy("WarpDashboard", policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin"));

app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapWarpUI("/warp").RequireAuthorization("WarpDashboard");
```

A DB-backed permission becomes an `AuthorizationHandler<T>`. For XHR, configure your scheme to answer
`/warp/api` paths with 401 rather than a redirect the SPA cannot follow; the SPA then reloads once so the
challenge lands on a navigation.

### Built-in login (host has no identity system)

Registers a real cookie authentication scheme; expiry is enforced server-side. `AddBuiltInLogin<T>`
registers the validator as scoped for you, and `AddDataProtection()` is not needed.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpDashboard().AddBuiltInLogin<MyCredentialValidator>();

app.MapWarpUI("/warp").RequireWarpDashboardLogin();
```

Registering the built-in login GATES the dashboard on its own — RequireWarpDashboardLogin() is explicit
rather than required, and is idempotent. Otherwise the half-configured shape (services registered,
convention forgotten) would render a login page over an anonymous API. Applying your own policy REPLACES the
login gate (it does not stack), and the SPA then reports hasBuiltInLogin=false.

```csharp
public class MyCredentialValidator : IWarpCredentialValidator
{
    private readonly AppDbContext _db;

    public MyCredentialValidator(AppDbContext db) => _db = db;

    public async Task<bool> ValidateAsync(string username, string password)
    {
        var user = await _db.Users.FirstOrDefaultAsync(u => u.Username == username);
        return user != null && BCrypt.Verify(password, user.PasswordHash);
    }
}
```

The built-in login gates the API and hub only — the SPA shell stays anonymous because it renders the login
form itself. `{prefix}/api/auth/status` is mapped ONLY with the built-in login: it is necessarily anonymous,
so mapping it always would bypass the host's gate and answer a constant `true`.

### Localhost only

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpDashboard();

app.MapWarpUI("/warp").RequireLocalRequests();
```

A remote caller gets 403 — signing in cannot change the answer. Covers shell, API and hub. The same
mechanism (pin `WarpDashboardDefaults.DenyScheme` on a policy) works for any rule signing in cannot
satisfy, even with no identity provider registered.

### What is gated

Everything under the route prefix: the SPA shell, its static assets (`/warp/assets/...`), dashboard
extension JS (`/warp/_ext/...`), the REST API and the SignalR hub. The dashboard's endpoints serve the
embedded assets themselves rather than UseStaticFiles, because StaticFileMiddleware stands down once
routing has matched an endpoint and the shell catch-all matches every asset path. Conditional requests
still work (304 on If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since).

Warp owns every path under the prefix: the shell's catch-all claims `{prefix}/{**path}`, so host content
served under the prefix by middleware is unreachable (a 4.0 break — move it outside the prefix; host
endpoints with literal routes still win). RoutePrefix is normalized ('/' + trim('/')) and the application
root is rejected. Every API response carries an `X-Warp-Api` header so the SPA can distinguish a genuine API
answer from a sign-in redirect it followed.

---

## Job Retention

- Completed/Deleted jobs: auto-expire after `JobExpirationTimeout` (default 1 day)
- Failed jobs: NEVER auto-expire (manual intervention required)
- Optional count-based cleanup: `MaxExpirableJobCount` deletes oldest by ExpireAt when threshold exceeded
- Statistics survive job deletion (persistent counters)
- Recurring job logs: last 100 per recurring job retained
- Observability call logs (adapter / webhook / endpoint) retain on **age AND count** — whichever trims first. Age via `*Retention` `TimeSpan`; count via `*RetentionCount` `int?` (null = off). Aggregate metrics (counts, error rate, average latency) survive log deletion.

---

## HTTP Endpoints (Moberg.Warp.Http)

Optional package that exposes `IRequest<TResponse>` and `IStreamRequest<TResponse>` handlers as ASP.NET Minimal API endpoints. Source-generated dispatch (no per-request reflection); independent of `Moberg.Warp.UI`. Handler binding is delegated to ASP.NET Minimal API — full support for `IParsable<T>`, `TryParse`, query arrays, route constraints, etc.

`IJob` and `IMessage` cannot be HTTP-exposed (compile-time error `WHTTP001`). The pattern for "submit a job via HTTP" is a thin `IRequest<Guid>` wrapper that calls `IPublisher.Enqueue`.

### Setup

```bash
dotnet add package Moberg.Warp.Http
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddWarpHttp();
app.MapWarpHttp();
```

### Defining endpoints — attribute on the handler class

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;          // [FromRoute], [FromQuery], [FromHeader], [FromBody]
using Warp.Core.Handlers;
using Warp.Http;

// Request type — public contract.
public sealed record GetOrder([FromRoute] Guid Id) : IRequest<OrderDto>;

// Handler class — carries the [WarpHttp...] attribute.
[WarpHttpGet("/orders/{id}")]
public sealed class GetOrderHandler : IRequestHandler<GetOrder, OrderDto>
{
    public Task<OrderDto> HandleAsync(GetOrder request, CancellationToken ct) { ... }
}
```

### Verb attributes

```csharp
[WarpHttpGet("/path")]      // GET
[WarpHttpPost("/path")]     // POST
[WarpHttpPut("/path")]      // PUT
[WarpHttpPatch("/path")]    // PATCH
[WarpHttpDelete("/path")]   // DELETE
```

### Response semantics

| Handler kind                  | Status | Body                                        |
|-------------------------------|--------|---------------------------------------------|
| `IRequest<TResponse>` non-Unit | 200    | JSON of `TResponse`                         |
| `IRequest<Unit>`              | 204    | empty                                       |
| `IStreamRequest<TResponse>`   | 200    | `text/event-stream` (one `data:` per item)  |

### Binding shapes

- **Whole-body** — body verb + no per-property attributes → ASP.NET binds whole `TRequest` from JSON body. Natural shape for plain POST DTOs.
- **AsParameters** — non-body verb (or no body part) → ASP.NET decomposes `TRequest` per `[FromRoute]` / `[FromQuery]` / `[FromHeader]` attributes via `[AsParameters]`. Records and classes both work; route-token names auto-bind on unattributed members.
- **Mixed** — request type has both `[FromBody]` and other source attributes → generator emits explicit lambda parameters per source and constructs `TRequest`. Use **classes with property setters** for mixed-binding cases (records' positional ctor attributes don't reach properties for `[AsParameters]`).

### Submit a job via HTTP

```csharp
public sealed record EnqueueReport(Guid TenantId) : IRequest<Guid>;

[WarpHttpPost("/reports/generate")]
public sealed class EnqueueReportHandler(IPublisher publisher)
    : IRequestHandler<EnqueueReport, Guid>
{
    public async Task<Guid> HandleAsync(EnqueueReport req, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var jobId = await publisher.Enqueue(new GenerateReportJob(req.TenantId));
        await publisher.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
        return jobId;
    }
}
```

### Streaming (SSE)

```csharp
public sealed record OrderEventFeed([FromQuery] Guid TenantId) : IStreamRequest<OrderEvent>;

[WarpHttpGet("/orders/feed")]
public sealed class OrderEventFeedHandler : IStreamRequestHandler<OrderEventFeed, OrderEvent>
{
    public async IAsyncEnumerable<OrderEvent> HandleAsync(
        OrderEventFeed request,
        [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct)
    {
        await foreach (var evt in _events.Subscribe(request.TenantId, ct))
            yield return evt;
    }
}
```

`HttpContext.RequestAborted` is plumbed to the handler — client disconnect cancels the enumeration.

### Auth

`[Authorize]` and `[AllowAnonymous]` on the handler class surface as ASP.NET endpoint metadata, composing with group-level `RequireAuthorization()`:

```csharp
[Authorize(Policy = "OrdersWrite")]
[WarpHttpPost("/orders")]
public sealed class CreateOrderHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateOrder, OrderDto> { ... }

// Override per endpoint:
[AllowAnonymous]
[WarpHttpGet("/api/health")]
public sealed class HealthCheckHandler : IRequestHandler<HealthCheck, HealthStatus> { ... }
```

### Named groups

```csharp
[WarpHttpPost("/orders", Group = "public")]
public sealed class CreateOrderPublicHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateOrder, OrderDto> { ... }

[WarpHttpPost("/admin/users", Group = "admin")]
public sealed class CreateAdminUserHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateAdminUser, Guid> { ... }
```

```csharp
app.MapWarpHttp();                                       // null-group descriptors
app.MapGroup("/api/public").RequireAuthorization("publicPolicy").MapWarpHttp("public");
app.MapGroup("/internal/admin").RequireAuthorization("adminPolicy").MapWarpHttp("admin");
```

`MapWarpHttp(group)` matches strictly. Double-call on the same builder + group throws `InvalidOperationException` at startup.

### Multi-attribute (versioning aliases)

```csharp
[WarpHttpPost("/v1/orders", Name = "CreateOrderV1")]
[WarpHttpPost("/v2/orders", Name = "CreateOrderV2")]
public sealed class CreateOrderHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateOrder, OrderDto> { ... }
```

`AllowMultiple = true` on `WarpHttpAttribute`; multi-attribute requires `Name` on each (`WHTTP002` if missing — ASP.NET requires unique route names).

### IHttpResponseShape

Response types implement `IHttpResponseShape` to override status / set headers / set Location:

```csharp
public sealed record CreatedOrder(Guid Id) : IHttpResponseShape
{
    public void Apply(HttpContext ctx)
    {
        ctx.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status201Created;
        ctx.Response.Headers.Location = $"/orders/{Id}";
    }
}
```

Apply runs after handler return, before body serialization. Only fires for `IRequest<TResponse>` non-Unit responses (not for `IRequest<Unit>` 204; not for streams).

### Diagnostics

| ID         | Severity | Condition |
|------------|----------|-----------|
| `WHTTP001` | Error    | Handler tagged with `[WarpHttp...]` either doesn't implement `IRequestHandler<,>` / `IStreamRequestHandler<,>`, or its request type implements `IJob` / `IMessage`. |
| `WHTTP002` | Error    | Handler has multiple `[WarpHttp...]` attributes but at least one is missing `Name = "..."`. |

### Pipeline behaviors

The HTTP path runs `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` — same chain as in-memory `IMediator.Send`. Auth, validation, logging behaviors apply for free. `RetryPipelineBehavior` (constraint `IJob`) and `MutexPipelineBehavior` (`is not IJob` runtime check) self-scope to the worker path and never run on HTTP.

### OpenAPI / Swagger

Endpoint metadata is populated automatically: `.Accepts<TRequest>("application/json")` on body verbs, `.Produces<TResponse>(200)` (or `.Produces(204)` for Unit), `.WithName(...)` from the attribute's Name, `.WithTags(...)` from the route's first segment. Swashbuckle / NSwag / `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` discover them transparently.

---

## Outbound Adapters (Moberg.Warp.Adapters)

Observes calls your app **makes to** other services — the mirror of the inbound `Warp.Http` binding. An adapter is a named outbound dependency (vendor API, SOAP service, payment gateway). Three layers:

1. **Protocol-agnostic core** (`Warp.Core.Adapters`) — `IWarpAdapters.BeginCall(adapter, operation, group?)` returns an `AdapterCallScope` (`Succeed`/`Fail`/`SetGroup`/`SetCorrelation`/`SetTag`) usable for any transport via manual scopes.
2. **HTTP binding** (`Warp.Adapters.Http`) — a `DelegatingHandler` that auto-scopes `IHttpClientFactory` clients; no retry dependency — bring your own via `ConfigureHttpClientBuilder`.
3. **Refit sugar** (`Warp.Adapters.Refit`) — operation names from `RestMethodInfo`.

**Telemetry is unconditional** (null-listener, zero cost without a listener): every completed scope emits a `Client` Activity named `{adapter}.{operation}` plus `warp.adapter.calls` / `warp.adapter.duration` meters, regardless of `AddAdapters()`. **Only DB call-log recording is gated by `opt.AddAdapters()`** (a bounded lossy channel + flusher; a full channel drops the record and increments `warp.adapter.records_dropped` — never blocks or fails a user call). Entities (`AdapterDefinition`, `AdapterCallLog`) are always in the schema.

**Three-axis identity:** adapter = policy + health boundary (registration-time); group = runtime who/where (destination, tenant — a runtime value, unbounded); operation = what (the API-contract axis, bounded). Litmus: swapping the value changes the request's *structure* → operation; only changes *where it goes / on whose behalf* → group.

**Cluster-shared rate limiter** — the differentiator per-process Polly cannot provide: same adapter name across the fleet shares one DB-backed token limit (`RateLimitBucket`, key `warp:adapter:{name}`). Shared-policy persistence is first-writer-wins; a later process whose local policy differs enforces the persisted policy, logs a Warning, and sets `HasPolicyConflict`. Change a shared limit via a `RateLimitOverride` admin row or by clearing the persisted policy — not by redeploying.

**Capture is opt-in and PII-owned:** metadata always; request bodies, response bodies, and headers each independently `None` / `OnFailure` / `Always`, truncated (`MaxCapturedBodySize` 8 KB / `MaxCapturedHeaderSize` 4 KB) and passed through the user-owned `RedactedHeaders` denylist (prepopulated with `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`X-Api-Key`/etc., fully overridable). Enums from 1: `CallRecording { All, FailuresOnly }`, `CaptureMode { None, OnFailure, Always }`, `AdapterCallOutcome { Success, Failed, Throttled, CircuitOpen }`.

```csharp
services.AddWarp<AppDb>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql(conn);
    opt.AddAdapters();                       // gates DB recording
    opt.AddAdapter("acme-payments", a =>
    {
        a.Recording.CaptureResponseBodies = CaptureMode.OnFailure;
        a.Recording.CallLogRetentionCount = 50_000;   // per-adapter count cap
        a.UseSharedRateLimit(perSeconds: 1, limit: 10);
    });
});
```

`Warp.Adapters.Http` wires the observing handler onto a named client; `Warp.Adapters.Refit` adds a typed client. Observe-first rollout: register with no resilience/rate-limit policy (zero behavioural change), read the data, add policy per adapter later. `IAdapterQueryService` is registered by `AddWarp` itself, so dashboard-only / publisher-only processes serve `/api/adapters*` without a server. Dashboard: `/warp/adapters`.

---

## Durable Webhooks (built into Moberg.Warp.Core)

Durable outbound webhook *delivery* is part of Core (`Warp.Core.Webhooks`) and **always on** — no package, no opt-in. `AddWarp` wires the dispatcher/executor/signer/redelivery-enqueuer and every `AddWarpServer` worker drains the `warp:webhooks` queue, so a delivery staged by any process is executed by any server (no per-process opt-in). `opt.AddWebhooks(...)` is optional config only (custom `IWebhookSigner`, exhausted-handler). Per-attempt `AdapterCallLog` rows require `AddAdapters()`; the delivery state machine works without it. **Boundary:** the host owns subscriptions, fan-out, payload building, and endpoint enable/disable; Warp owns everything after `IWebhookDispatcher.SendAsync(WebhookSend)` — delivery lifecycle, retry scheduling, signing, redelivery, exhaustion, dashboard.

**The delivery, not the job, is the state machine.** The executor (an ordinary source-gen job on queue `warp:webhooks`) always completes; every attempt exception is caught and recorded as an attempt failure — webhook failures never surface as failed jobs. State lives on the always-in-schema `WebhookDelivery` row: `WebhookDeliveryStatus { Pending, Delivered, Exhausted }`. The row is self-contained (URL, headers, payload, schedule, success codes, signing mode + secret) stamped at `SendAsync` time, so a later config deploy never reshapes an in-flight delivery. `SendAsync` persists `Pending` + enqueues the first attempt in the caller's transaction (outbox) and returns the delivery id.

**Attempts are adapter calls** through the auto-registered `warp-webhooks` adapter (group = endpoint, operation = event type, `CorrelationId` = delivery id; response bodies always captured, request bodies never — the payload is already on the row). The attempt timeline is `AdapterCallLog WHERE CorrelationId = deliveryId` — no separate attempt table.

**No timers/scans:** each retry is a fresh executor job in `State.Scheduled` at `now + schedule[N]` riding `ScheduledJobActivation`. `RetrySchedule` is per-send `IReadOnlyList<TimeSpan>?`: `null` = built-in `[1m, 10m, 1h, 6h]`, `[]` = single attempt then `Exhausted`. Cadence is delay + up to ~5s activation + worker pickup — a backoff, not a precision scheduler.

**Signing** (`WebhookSigning { None, StandardWebhooks, Custom }`): `StandardWebhooks` = HMAC-SHA256 over `{id}.{timestamp}.{payload}` with `webhook-id`/`webhook-timestamp`/`webhook-signature` headers; `Custom` = a registered `IWebhookSigner` via `w.UseCustomSigner<T>()` (declaring `Custom` without a signer throws at `AddWebhooks` time). Secrets are stored on the row for self-containment but redacted on every read surface. `IWebhookCommandService.Redeliver(id)` requeues a settled delivery. Exhaustion invokes the host's `IWebhookDeliveryExhaustedHandler` at-least-once, post-commit. Retention: age (`WebhookDeliveryRetention`, default 30d) + count (`WebhookDeliveryRetentionCount`).

**Prerequisite:** a Warp server (worker) must run somewhere to drain `warp:webhooks` — coexists with another job system. `IWebhookQueryService` / `IWebhookCommandService` resolve in any `AddWarp` process. Dashboard: `/warp/webhooks`.

```csharp
opt.AddWebhooks(w => w.OnDeliveryExhausted<MyExhaustedHandler>());
// inside your transaction:
var id = await dispatcher.SendAsync(new WebhookSend
{
    Url = endpoint.Url, EventType = "order.created", Payload = json,
    Signing = WebhookSigning.StandardWebhooks, Secret = endpoint.Secret,
    RetrySchedule = null,   // built-in backoff
});
```

---

## Inbound Endpoint Observability (Moberg.Warp.Http)

The inbound mirror of adapters: observes requests **made to** your Warp HTTP endpoints (handlers exposed via `MapWarpHttp`). Opt in with `opt.AddEndpointObservability(o => ...)` inside the `AddWarp` lambda **and** `app.UseWarpHttpObservability()` after `UseRouting()`. The middleware no-ops unless the matched endpoint carries `WarpEndpointIdentity` — it never observes your own controllers, the dashboard, health, or static files.

**Identity = HTTP method + route TEMPLATE** (`GET /orders/{id}`) — already bounded (inline constraints normalized: `{id:int}` → `{id}`), no path-cardinality heuristic. Counter dimensions are Total + optional low-cardinality Group (from `o.GroupSelector(HttpContext)` — a channel/client/tenant key, never raw IP/user id).

**Capture (PII):** caller IP (`RemoteIpAddress`, or first `X-Forwarded-For` hop when `UseForwardedForIp`), user-agent, and `User.Identity.Name` are captured by default (the point of the feature) but are PII — redactable/disableable, never logged Info+. Request/response bodies + headers each `None` / `OnFailure` / `Always` (default `OnFailure`), truncated and redacted through the same `RedactedHeaders` denylist as adapters. `CaptureBodyStream` never buffers a whole streaming/`IResult` response.

**Outcome:** `Failed` = status ≥ 500 or an unhandled exception; **4xx is counted Success** (client error) so the error rate stays a meaningful server-health signal. `RecordCalls = FailuresOnly` skips success ROWS only (counters still written). Recording is lossy and never blocks/fails the request. Retention is global on `WarpConfiguration.EndpointCallLogRetention` (age, default 7d) + `EndpointCallLogRetentionCount` (count). `IEndpointQueryService` is registered by `AddWarp`, so dashboard-only processes serve `/api/endpoints*` without the middleware. Dashboard: `/warp/endpoints`.

```csharp
opt.AddEndpointObservability(o =>
{
    o.CaptureResponseBodies = CaptureMode.OnFailure;
    o.UseForwardedForIp = true;
    o.GroupSelector = ctx => ctx.Request.Headers["X-Client"].FirstOrDefault();
});
// after app.UseRouting():
app.UseWarpHttpObservability();
```

---

## DI Services Available

After calling `AddWarp<TContext>()` or `AddWarpServer<TContext>()`, these services are available via dependency injection:

| Service | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `IPublisher` | Enqueue jobs, publish messages, schedule jobs |
| `IMediator` | Send in-memory requests |
| `IBatchPublisher` | Create batches with continuations |
| `IRecurringJobPublisher` | Register/update recurring job definitions |
| `IJobQueryService` | Query jobs, job details, traces |
| `IJobCommandService` | Delete, requeue, bulk operations on jobs |
| `IJobGroupQueryService` | Query messages and batches |
| `IRecurringJobService` | Trigger, delete recurring jobs, query history |
| `IDashboardStatsService` | Dashboard statistics, server/worker info |
| `IJobContext` | Current job's ID, trace ID, and metadata (available inside handlers) |
| `IServerCommandService` | Pause/resume servers and worker groups |
| `IAdapterQueryService` | Query outbound-adapter stats, call logs, history (registered by AddWarp) |
| `IEndpointQueryService` | Query inbound-endpoint stats, call logs (registered by AddWarp) |
| `IWebhookQueryService` / `IWebhookCommandService` | Query webhook deliveries; redeliver a settled delivery (registered by AddWarp) |
| `IWebhookDispatcher` | Send a durable webhook delivery (always registered by `AddWarp`) |
| `TimeProvider` | Injectable time (registered as `TimeProvider.System` by default, override in tests) |

---

## Public API Reference

### Handler Interfaces

```csharp
// Base request — all types implement this
public interface IRequest<out TResponse>;

// Job marker — persistent, single handler
public interface IJob : IRequest<Unit>;

// Message marker — persistent, multiple handlers
public interface IMessage : IRequest<Unit>;

// Handler for jobs
public interface IJobHandler<in T> where T : IJob
{
    Task HandleAsync(T message, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

// Handler for messages
public interface IMessageHandler<in T> where T : IMessage
{
    Task HandleAsync(T message, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

// Handler for requests
public interface IRequestHandler<in TRequest, TResponse> where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
{
    Task<TResponse> HandleAsync(TRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

// Pipeline behavior — wraps all handler types
public interface IPipelineBehavior<in TRequest, TResponse> where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
{
    Task<TResponse> HandleAsync(TRequest request, RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}
```

### IJobContext & IJobMetadata

```csharp
public interface IJobMetadata
{
    IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> Metadata { get; }
}

public interface IJobContext : IJobMetadata
{
    Guid JobId { get; }
    Guid TraceId { get; }
}
```

### IPublishPipelineBehavior

```csharp
public class PublishContext<T> : IJobMetadata
{
    public required T Job { get; init; }
    public Dictionary<string, string> Metadata { get; init; } = new();
}

public interface IPublishPipelineBehavior<T>
{
    Task PublishAsync(PublishContext<T> context, PublishDelegate next, CancellationToken ct);
}
```

### IPublisher

The most common overloads are shown below. For full control, use the `JobParameters` overload which accepts all options in a single call.

```csharp
public interface IPublisher
{
    // Messages (pub/sub)
    Task<Guid> Publish<T>(T message) where T : class, IMessage;
    Task<Guid> Publish<T>(T message, string? queue) where T : class, IMessage;

    // Jobs — common overloads (additional combinations of maxRetries, queue, parentJobId exist)
    Task<Guid> Enqueue<T>(T job) where T : class, IJob;
    Task<Guid> Enqueue<T>(T job, int maxRetries) where T : class, IJob;
    Task<Guid> Enqueue<T>(T job, Guid parentJobId) where T : class, IJob;
    Task<Guid> Enqueue<T>(T job, string queue) where T : class, IJob;
    Task<Guid> Enqueue<T>(T job, JobParameters parameters) where T : class, IJob;  // Full control
    Task<Guid> Schedule<T>(T job, DateTime scheduleTime) where T : class, IJob;

    Task SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

Note: `publisher.SaveChangesAsync()` and `context.SaveChangesAsync()` flush the same underlying DbContext — they are interchangeable. Use whichever is available. The outbox pattern examples use `context.SaveChangesAsync()` to emphasize that jobs and business data are committed together.

### IMediator

```csharp
public interface IMediator
{
    Task<TResponse> Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

### IBatchPublisher

```csharp
public interface IBatchPublisher
{
    Task<Guid> StartNew<T>(List<T> jobs, string? name = null, ContinuationOptions options = ContinuationOptions.OnlyOnSucceeded) where T : class, IJob;
    Task<Guid> ContinueBatchWith<T>(List<T> jobs, Guid parentId, string? name = null, ContinuationOptions options = ContinuationOptions.OnlyOnSucceeded) where T : class, IJob;
    Task SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

### IRecurringJobPublisher

```csharp
public interface IRecurringJobPublisher
{
    Task AddOrUpdateRecurringJob<T>(T message, string name, string cron) where T : class, IJob;
}
```

### IWarpCredentialValidator

public interface IWarpCredentialValidator

    Task<bool> ValidateAsync(string username, string password);
}
```

### Enums

public enum State { Enqueued = 1, Awaiting = 2, Processing = 3, Completed = 4, Failed = 5, Deleted = 6 }
public enum ContinuationOptions { OnlyOnSucceeded = 1, OnAnyFinishedState = 2 }
public enum JobKind { Job = 1, Message = 2, Batch = 3 }

```

### Extension Methods

```csharp
// Core registration. Throws InvalidOperationException at AddWarp time if TContext is
// not registered as Scoped (most common cause: AddDbContextFactory<T> without AddDbContext<T>).
IServiceCollection.AddWarp<TContext>();
IServiceCollection.AddWarp<TContext>(Action<WarpBuilder<TContext>> configure);

// Worker registration (includes AddWarp internally)
IServiceCollection.AddWarpServer<TContext>();
IServiceCollection.AddWarpServer<TContext>(Action<WarpServerBuilder<TContext>> configure);

// Addon opt-ins on the builder lambda parameter (IWarpBuilder<TContext>)
opt.UsePostgreSql() / opt.UseSqlServer();    // required provider opt-in
opt.AddRetry(Action<RetryOptions>);
opt.AddTimeout(Action<TimeoutOptions>);
opt.AddConcurrency();
opt.AddCircuitBreaker(Action<CircuitBreakerOptions>);
opt.AddRateLimit();
opt.AddNoRestart();
opt.AddSagas();
opt.UseDatabasePush();
opt.AddDashboardPush();
opt.AddBackgroundService<T>();               // register a WarpBackgroundService (base feature)
opt.DisableWorker();                         // service-only server (no job worker)
opt.AddAdapters();                           // gate outbound-adapter DB recording
opt.AddAdapter(name, Action<WarpAdapterOptions>);
opt.AddWebhooks(Action<WarpWebhookOptions>); // OPTIONAL webhook config (custom signer / exhausted-handler); delivery is always on
opt.AddEndpointObservability(Action<WarpEndpointObservabilityOptions>); // inbound endpoint observability
opt.ExcludeHandlersFromAssembly(Assembly);   // multi-host opt-out — see Multi-Project page

// Handlers and pipeline behaviors are source-gen registered — no AddJobHandlers / AddPipelineBehaviors
// extension methods exist. Define a class implementing the handler/behavior interface and build.

// Dashboard
WebApplication.MapWarpUI(string routePrefix);
WebApplication.MapWarpUI(Action<WarpUIOptions> setupAction);
WarpUIEndpointConventionBuilder.RequireWarpDashboardLogin();
WarpUIEndpointConventionBuilder.RequireLocalRequests();
IServiceCollection.AddWarpDashboard().AddBuiltInLogin<TValidator>();

// Inbound endpoint observability middleware (after UseRouting) — pairs with opt.AddEndpointObservability()
IApplicationBuilder.UseWarpHttpObservability();
```

---

## Common Patterns

### Controller with all three patterns

```csharp
public class OrderController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IPublisher _publisher;
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;
    private readonly AppDbContext _context;

    public OrderController(IPublisher publisher, IMediator mediator, AppDbContext context)
    {
        _publisher = publisher;
        _mediator = mediator;
        _context = context;
    }

    [HttpPost]
    public async Task<IActionResult> CreateOrder(CreateOrderRequest request)
    {
        // In-memory request for validation
        var isValid = await _mediator.Send(new ValidateOrder { Data = request });
        if (!isValid) return BadRequest();

        var order = new Order { CustomerId = request.CustomerId };
        _context.Orders.Add(order);

        // Background job
        await _publisher.Enqueue(new SendConfirmationEmail { OrderId = order.Id });

        // Pub/sub message — multiple handlers
        await _publisher.Publish(new OrderPlaced { OrderId = order.Id });

        // All committed atomically
        await _context.SaveChangesAsync();
        return Ok(order.Id);
    }
}
```

### Validation pipeline behavior

```csharp
public class ValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
{
    private readonly IEnumerable<IValidator<TRequest>> _validators;

    public ValidationBehavior(IEnumerable<IValidator<TRequest>> validators) => _validators = validators;

    public async Task<TResponse> HandleAsync(
        TRequest request,
        RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next,
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var failures = _validators
            .Select(v => v.Validate(request))
            .SelectMany(r => r.Errors)
            .Where(f => f != null)
            .ToList();

        if (failures.Count > 0)
            throw new ValidationException(failures);

        return await next();
    }
}
```

### Batch with continuation

```csharp
public async Task ProcessMonthlyReports(List<int> months)
{
    var jobs = months.Select(m => new GenerateReport { Month = m }).ToList();
    var batchId = await _batchPublisher.StartNew(jobs, options: ContinuationOptions.OnAnyFinishedState);

    var summary = new List<SendReportSummary> { new() };
    await _batchPublisher.ContinueBatchWith(summary, batchId);

    await _batchPublisher.SaveChangesAsync();
    // All individual reports run in parallel, then SendReportSummary fires when all finish
}
```

### Separate publisher and worker apps

Publisher app (web API):

```csharp
// Only creates jobs, doesn't process them
builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseNpgsql(connStr));
builder.Services.AddWarp<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();
    // Optional: if the publisher project references a worker-only assembly transitively
    // and you don't want worker handlers in this process's DI graph:
    // opt.ExcludeHandlersFromAssembly(typeof(WorkerOnlyMarker).Assembly);
});
```

Worker app (background service):

```csharp
// Only processes jobs
builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseNpgsql(connStr));
builder.Services.AddWarpServer<AppDbContext>(opt =>
{
    opt.UsePostgreSql();
    opt.WorkerCount = 20;
    opt.Queues = ["default"];
});
```

Both apps share the same database. The worker polls for and executes jobs created by the publisher. Handlers are picked up by the source generator in whichever project defines them and replayed into the host's DI graph by `AddWarp` / `AddWarpServer` — no `AddJobHandlers(asm)` calls.

---

## Key Design Rules

1. **DbContext must be Scoped** (not Transient) — required for the outbox pattern to work
2. **Call SaveChangesAsync()** after publishing — jobs are not committed until you save
3. **Failed jobs never auto-delete** — they persist until manually handled
4. **Queue order is alphabetical** — use prefixes like "a-", "b-", "c-" for priority
5. **AddWarpServer includes AddWarp** — don't call both
6. **MapWarpUI + RequireAuthorization** — gate the dashboard with an ASP.NET policy, not a bool filter
7. **TimeProvider is injectable** — use it for testability, Warp registers TimeProvider.System by default
8. **Handler ILogger output is captured** — logs are flushed every ~1s and appear in the dashboard in real time
9. **Job metadata is inherited** — child jobs automatically inherit parent metadata via ambient context
10. **Pause is propagated via heartbeat** — there may be a ~3s delay between pause command and workers stopping
11. **Warp tables use the `warp` schema by default** — configurable via `WarpConfiguration.Schema`, set to `null` for default schema
12. **Naming conventions are respected** — entity configs don't hardcode table/column names, so `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()` works
